Branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO) is plausible given sectoral vision loss possibility, though patient describes complete right-eye loss—still possible if large branch involved or misperception of field defect; lower confidence than CRAO due to less common presentation of total vision loss. Excluded: giant cell arteritis (GCA) — high suspicion would require age >50 + systemic symptoms (e.g., headache, jaw claudication, scalp tenderness), not mentioned; also GCA-related vision loss is often preceded by transient visual obscurations and is rarely truly painless due to associated systemic inflammation. Also excluded: vitreous hemorrhage or retinal detachment—typically associated with floaters, flashes, or progressive loss, not abrupt total loss."}
